overall_summary: Bitcoin faces clear headwinds from heavy ETF outflows and a much stronger jobs report that reduces near-term rate-cut odds. A firmer dollar and elevated geopolitical risks add pressure, while whale accumulation and 401(k) progress provide only limited offsets. Tuesday’s CPI remains the next major catalyst traders will watch.
key_points: Strong NFP cools Fed cut expectations

items.title: Bitcoin ETFs See $1.28B Weekly Outflows, Flip 2026 Negative
items.summary: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded about $1.28 billion in net outflows last week, the worst since June, pushing year-to-date flows deeply negative at roughly $914 million. BlackRock's IBIT alone saw hundreds of millions leave on Friday. Traders should care because this is the clearest signal of institutional demand drying up amid the recent selloff and macro pressure from jobs data and tech weakness. Sustained outflows remove a key bid under Bitcoin near the $75,000-$76,000 zone.
items.impact: Adds selling pressure and weakens near-term support

items.title: Binance Hackers Swap $175M Alts Into 2,300 BTC
items.summary: Blockchain firm Elliptic reports the attackers behind the record $6.3 billion Binance theft have now converted roughly $175 million in stolen altcoins into about 2,300 Bitcoin, up sharply from the prior day. Activity spans tens of thousands of wallets and multiple chains, with most original stolen BTC still sitting untouched. This matters because large-scale conversion into Bitcoin can create supply overhang if the coins are later sold, keeping risk premium elevated for the whole market while Binance restores services.
items.impact: Potential future sell pressure and lingering security overhang

items.title: US Treasury Cuts MEXC Off From American Banking System
items.summary: FinCEN issued an order severing crypto exchange MEXC Global from the U.S. financial system, citing at least $16 billion in alleged illicit flows tied to Russian, Iranian and North Korean sanctions evasion. U.S. banks and money transmitters will be barred from processing transfers once the order takes effect. Traders should watch this because it raises compliance costs and de-risking risks across offshore exchanges, potentially reducing liquidity and amplifying regulatory headlines that weigh on sentiment.
items.impact: Heightens exchange risk and regulatory overhang

items.title: Dormant Whale Accumulates 3,009 BTC Worth $228 Million
items.summary: A Bitcoin address inactive for more than a year withdrew and accumulated 3,009 BTC valued around $228 million from Binance on November 6 at prices near $75,800. On-chain trackers flagged the multi-tranche buy as the wallet's first major activity in over a year after previously depositing coins higher. This is relevant because large smart-money accumulation during a dip often signals conviction buying that can stabilize price or front-run a rebound if other whales follow.
items.impact: Supports price floor via large-holder demand

items.title: Russia Clears Retail BTC, ETH, USDT Trading From November 17
items.summary: The Bank of Russia has approved Bitcoin, Ether and USDT for non-qualified retail investors starting November 17, with a 300,000-ruble annual cap per intermediary and mandatory risk testing. Moscow Exchange plans pilot trading of the same assets from December 1. Traders should care because this opens a large new regulated market in a major economy, potentially adding fresh demand and legitimizing crypto access even under capital controls.
items.impact: Expands global retail access and adoption narrative

items.title: Crypto 401(k) Safe-Harbor Rule Enters Final White House Review
items.summary: The Labor Department's final rule creating a fiduciary safe harbor for adding alternative assets including crypto funds to 401(k) menus has arrived at the White House Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs for last-step review. The framework follows a Trump executive order and earlier proposal outlining evaluation factors like fees, liquidity and complexity. This could unlock significant long-term inflows from the multi-trillion-dollar retirement market if finalized, giving Bitcoin a structural demand tailwind beyond spot ETFs.

items.title: October NFP Surges 165K, Far Above Forecasts
items.summary: US employers added 165,000 jobs in October, crushing expectations around 65,000, while unemployment fell to 4.1 percent. Prior months were revised up by a combined 84,000, and wages rose 0.4 percent month-over-month. This strength keeps the labor market tight and has pushed markets to price roughly an 80 percent chance of a December Fed hike, lifting the dollar and Treasury yields on Friday. Crypto traders should care because stronger growth data typically means higher-for-longer rates and tighter liquidity, which has weighed on Bitcoin near recent supports.
items.impact: Raises Dec rate-hike odds and supports firmer USD/yields, pressuring risk assets

items.title: October CPI Looms Tuesday as Key Fed Test
items.summary: The next major US inflation print lands Tuesday at 8:30 AM ET, with economists looking for a cooler 0.2 to 0.3 percent month-over-month rise after September's hot 0.6 percent jump. Core is expected around 0.2 percent. This is the last big CPI before the December FOMC and will decide whether December hike bets stick or ease after the strong jobs number. Traders need to watch it closely because a hotter print reinforces hawkish Fed pricing while a soft one could reopen room for risk assets including Bitcoin.
items.impact: High-volatility catalyst for rates, DXY, and crypto direction this week

items.title: Dollar Rebounds to 102.28 as Yields Firm
items.summary: The US Dollar Index closed Friday near 102.28 after the strong jobs data, reversing some of the post-midterm weakness that had taken it toward five-week lows around 101. The 10-year Treasury yield held near 4.86 to 4.87 percent. A firmer dollar and higher real yields tighten global financial conditions. For crypto this usually means headwinds as liquidity preference shifts away from risk assets until the next data clears the picture.
items.impact: Stronger DXY and yields act as near-term drag on Bitcoin and equities

items.title: Democratic Midterm Sweep Sparks Fiscal Gridlock Bets
items.summary: Democrats took both chambers of Congress in the November 3 midterms, creating divided government under President Trump. Markets initially read this as limiting big new spending or tax cuts, which helped pull Treasury yields lower and weighed on the dollar earlier in the week before jobs data reversed part of the move. The setup reduces tail risks of unchecked deficits but leaves debt-ceiling and funding fights ahead. Crypto traders watch because lower long-term yield pressure can eventually support risk assets if the Fed path softens.
items.impact: Potential ceiling on fiscal stimulus and yields, mixed near-term for risk

items.title: UMich Sentiment Rises, Inflation Expectations Ease
items.summary: University of Michigan preliminary November consumer sentiment jumped to 51.0 from 48.0, beating forecasts, while one-year inflation expectations fell to 4.3 percent from 4.7 percent and longer-run edged to 3.4 percent. The survey was mostly pre-election. Easing inflation views are a mild positive for the soft-landing narrative even as cost-of-living complaints remain high. This offers a small counterweight to the hot jobs data ahead of CPI and could temper the most hawkish rate bets if confirmed.
items.impact: Softens inflation-fear premium slightly, limited immediate market move

items.title: Bank of England Hikes to 4 Percent, Signals More Possible
items.summary: The Bank of England raised Bank Rate by 25 basis points to 4 percent on November 5 in an 8-1 vote, its first hike in three years, citing pipeline inflation from elevated energy prices tied to Middle East conflict. Officials warned inflation could approach 5 percent next year and left the door open to further tightening. This adds to the global picture of central banks still fighting sticky prices. For crypto it reinforces a higher-rate world outside the US as well, keeping liquidity conditions relatively tight.
items.impact: Supports global higher-for-longer theme and firm USD crosses

items.title: Iran Lifts 2,000km Ballistic Missile Range Cap
items.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard announced it has scrapped its long-standing self-imposed limit on ballistic missile ranges, saying the restriction is lifted and capabilities will be proven in action. This comes days after the supreme leader ordered responses without geographic limits and amid ongoing US-Iran hostilities. Traders should watch closely because longer-range threats raise escalation risk across the Middle East and Europe, supporting higher oil prices and broader risk-off pressure on equities and crypto.
items.impact: Elevates oil risk premium and geopolitical risk-off for risk assets

items.title: US Disables Cargo Ship Breaking Iran Naval Blockade
items.summary: US Central Command confirmed an aircraft fired precision munitions at the stern of the St. Kitts-flagged M/V Huda in the Gulf of Oman after it ignored warnings and tried to leave after visiting an Iranian port. CENTCOM also launched Task Force Iron Gate to choke land and Caspian routes for weapons and illicit cargo. This tightens the energy choke on Iran and keeps Hormuz tensions high, which can spike oil and weigh on risk appetite including Bitcoin.
items.impact: Sustains oil supply fears and risk-off flows

items.title: Qatar Plan Could Reopen Strait of Hormuz Fast
items.summary: Qatar is mediating a proposal where the US lifts its naval blockade and releases some frozen Iranian assets in exchange for IAEA inspectors accessing bombed nuclear sites, with Iran reopening the Strait of Hormuz on day two via an Oman-agreed route. The Emir has spoken with Trump and Iranian officials are reviewing. A credible de-escalation path would ease the biggest energy shock since the 1970s, potentially crushing oil prices and lifting risk assets, though acceptance remains uncertain.
items.impact: Deal hopes could cut oil premium; failure keeps pressure high

items.title: Russia Hits Kyiv with 36 Ballistic Missiles
items.summary: Russia launched waves of ballistic missiles including Iskanders and reportedly North Korean types plus over 170 drones overnight, heavily damaging Kyiv-area energy substations linked to nuclear plants, the Northern Bridge, and civilian sites. Only a handful of missiles were intercepted amid interceptor shortages; several people were wounded. The barrage comes days before US-mediated Abu Dhabi talks, signaling Moscow is negotiating from strength by blacking out infrastructure ahead of winter.
items.impact: Adds energy and escalation risk ahead of peace talks

items.title: Herzog Tasks Eisenkot to Form Israeli Government
items.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog has given former IDF chief Gadi Eisenkot of the Yashar party the first mandate to assemble a coalition after the deadlocked October election. Eisenkot received more Knesset recommendations than Netanyahu and has 28 days, extendable, to secure a majority. A shift away from Netanyahu's hardline bloc could alter Israel's approach to Iran, Gaza, and the US alliance, introducing policy uncertainty for the region.
items.impact: Political uncertainty in key US ally; potential ME policy shift

items.title: Paraguay Impeaches President Peña Over Bank Collapse
items.summary: Paraguay's Senate unanimously impeached President Santiago Peña and placed him under house arrest after the collapse of Ueno Bank, a major digital lender with past ties to him that froze accounts for millions. Vice President Pedro Alliana was sworn in as replacement. The rapid ouster of a US-aligned leader over financial scandal highlights Latin American political and banking fragility that can spill into regional risk sentiment.
items.impact: Local political shock; limited direct global market spillover
